title: The pullback tensor comparison on the homotopy category
statement: Let $\Lambda$ be a commutative condensed ring [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring] and $f\colon X\to Y$ a morphism of schemes. Write $\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ for module objects over the pulled-back ring on the pro-étale site of $T$, $f^*$ for the (exact, monoidal) pullback of module objects, $Lf^*$ for its left derived functor and $\otimes^L$ for the derived tensor product [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull, sk-def-sfb-derived-tensor-hom]; $Q_h\colon K(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})\to D(\Mod_{\Lambda_T})$ is the localization of the homotopy category. The maps $Q_h(f^*A)\otimes^LQ_h(f^*B)\to Q_h(f^*A\otimes f^*B)\to Q_h(f^*(A\otimes B))$, the lax monoidal structure of $Q_h$ followed by $Q_h$ of the degreewise tensor comparison $f^*A\otimes f^*B\cong f^*(A\otimes B)$ of complexes, form a natural transformation of bifunctors on $K(\Mod_{\Lambda_Y})$ (natural in $A$ and in $B$).

proof.text: Put $\mathcal C_T=\Mod_{\Lambda_T}$ and $F=f^*$. The small pro-étale sites are essentially small in the coefficient universe, as specified in [sk-def-sfb-sheaf-tensor], whose sheafified objectwise tensor is the one used for module objects. For abelian sheaves this tensor category is closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian by [lem-weil-pbc-sheaf-tensor-closed]. Abelian groups have a functorial flat resolution by [lem-sfb-abelian-functorial-flat-resolution], so $\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ has one by [lem-sfb-sheaf-functorial-flat-resolution]. Apply [lem-sfb-modobj-grothendieck] and [def-sfb-modobj-internal-hom] to the commutative ring object $\Lambda_T$: $\mathcal C_T$ is Grothendieck abelian and closed symmetric monoidal for the relative tensor, and by [lem-sfb-modobj-flat-resolutions] it has a functorial flat resolution for that tensor. Its tensor functors are left adjoints, so preserve small colimits by [lem-weil-pbc-left-adjoint-preserves-colimits]. They are additive: preservation of zero objects and binary coproducts gives preservation of biproduct projections and diagonals, hence of $a+b=\nabla(a\oplus b)\Delta$. The functor $F$ is additive by [def-sfb-module-upper-star], a left adjoint by [sk-def-sfb-module-pushforward-pullback], and strong monoidal on the actual internal-module category by the first assertion of [new-integral-residue-ordinary-monoidal]. The same colimit theorem makes $F$ preserve countable coproducts. Thus the hypotheses of the termwise tensor comparison are satisfied, with no boundedness or flatness assumption on the complexes, and $\Sh(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ and $\mathcal C_T$ satisfy the hypotheses of the relative derived tensor and of the lax monoidal localization used in step 4. The ordinary strong structure uses the existing mapMod structure [def-sfb-mapmod-strong-monoidal] and extension/restriction along the coefficient isomorphism [def-sfb-comap-iso-strong-monoidal].

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-termwise-strong-monoidal] to $F$. Let $m_{A,B}=\tau_{A,B}^{-1}:F_{\rm Ch}A\otimes F_{\rm Ch}B\to F_{\rm Ch}(A\otimes B)$. This is a chain isomorphism natural in both complexes. Its degree-$n$ map is exactly the map in the item: writing $\iota_{p,q}$ and $\iota'_{p,q}$ for the total-tensor summand inclusions, the defining equation $\tau^n F(\iota_{p,q})=\iota'_{p,q}c_{A^p,B^q}$ gives $m^n\iota'_{p,q}=F(\iota_{p,q})\mu^F_{A^p,B^q}$ after composing with the inverses. Equality on all direct-sum inclusions determines the degree map. In particular this identifies $m$ with the concrete degreewise comparison using the existing proved chain-map equation. The already proved chain-map property [lem-sfb-upper-star-tensor-complex-comparison-chain-map] supplies the specified concrete complex morphism, whose components are identified by this calculation.

proof.text:
The homotopy category and its tensor are those of [lem-sfb-total-tensor-homotopy]. Termwise $F$ sends a cochain homotopy $a-a'=dh+hd$ to $F(a)-F(a')=dF(h)+F(h)d$ by additivity, so gives a functor $F_h$ on homotopy classes. Define $\bar m_{A,B}$ to be the homotopy class of $m_{A,B}$. For classes $a:A\to A'$ and $b:B\to B'$, choose cochain-map representatives. Complex naturality from step 2 gives
$$F_h(a\otimes b)\circ\bar m_{A,B}=\bar m_{A',B'}\circ(F_ha\otimes F_hb).$$
Passing the equality to classes is legitimate because the quotient is strong monoidal and its tensor on maps is induced from complexes. The equation is independent of the representatives by the very definition of a quotient morphism. Thus $\bar m$ is a natural tensor comparison on $K(\mathcal C_Y)$.

proof.text:
By step 1, $\mathcal C_X$ is a closed symmetric monoidal Grothendieck abelian category with additive tensor and a functorial flat resolution, over the ambient $\Sh(X_{\mathrm{proét}},\Ab)$ with the same properties. By [def-sfb-derived-tensor-modules] the tensor on $D(\mathcal C_X)$ is the relative derived tensor, obtained by the construction of [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal]. The latter states that $Q_h:K(\mathcal C_X)\to D(\mathcal C_X)$ is lax monoidal. Write $\mu_{U,V}:Q_hU\otimes^LQ_hV\to Q_h(U\otimes V)$ for its tensorator; it is natural in $U,V$ as part of the lax monoidal structure. Define
$$\theta_{A,B}=Q_h(\bar m_{A,B})\circ\mu_{F_hA,F_hB}.$$
Both factors have the indicated source and target, so this is the component displayed in the item, in the same coefficient category.

proof.text:
For $a:A\to A'$ and $b:B\to B'$ in $K(\mathcal C_Y)$, use the equation of step 3 and functoriality of $Q_h$, then naturality of its lax tensorator from [lem-sfb-derived-monoidal], to compute
$$\begin{aligned}
Q_h(F_h(a\otimes b))\circ\theta_{A,B}
&=Q_h(\bar m_{A',B'})\circ Q_h(F_ha\otimes F_hb)\circ\mu_{F_hA,F_hB}\\
&=Q_h(\bar m_{A',B'})\circ\mu_{F_hA',F_hB'}\circ(Q_h(F_ha)\otimes^LQ_h(F_hb))\\
&=\theta_{A',B'}\circ(Q_h(F_ha)\otimes^LQ_h(F_hb)).
\end{aligned}$$
Taking $a=1_A$ gives naturality in $B$; taking $b=1_B$ gives naturality in $A$. For the curried bifunctors, the first identity makes each $\theta_{A,-}$ a natural transformation and the second is the componentwise equality asserting naturality of $A\mapsto\theta_{A,-}$. Thus the displayed components define the required natural transformation of bifunctors. The Lean implementation identifies each concrete quotient map with the component of the inverse termwise oplax natural transformation, using mapHomotopyCategoryδNatTrans_app_app and the existing complex-comparison equation. It then applies naturality of that inverse transformation and of the lax tensorator of Qh, separately in each variable. These equations fill precisely the two original naturality fields.

noncomputable def upperStarTensorCounit :
    (((whiskeringLeft₂ _).obj
        ((f)^*⟦Λ⟧.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)).obj
        ((f)^*⟦Λ⟧.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)).obj
        (curriedTensor _) ⟶
      upperStarTensorTarget Λ f where
  app A :=
    { app B := Functor.LaxMonoidal.μ DerivedCategory.Qh
          (((f)^*⟦Λ⟧.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj A)
          (((f)^*⟦Λ⟧.mapHomotopyCategory (ComplexShape.up ℤ)).obj B) ≫
        DerivedCategory.Qh.map ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).map
          (upperStarTensorComplexHom Λ f A.as B.as))
      naturality B B' ψ := by
        obtain ⟨A, rfl⟩ := A.quotient_obj_surjective
        obtain ⟨B, rfl⟩ := B.quotient_obj_surjective
        obtain ⟨B', rfl⟩ := B'.quotient_obj_surjective
        obtain ⟨ψ, rfl⟩ := (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).map_surjective ψ
        have h := upperStarTensorCounit_naturality_aux Λ f (𝟙 A) ψ
        rw [CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id,
          CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, MonoidalCategory.id_tensorHom,
          MonoidalCategory.id_tensorHom] at h
        rw [Category.assoc]
        exact h }
  naturality A A' φ := by
    ext B
    obtain ⟨A, rfl⟩ := A.quotient_obj_surjective
    obtain ⟨A', rfl⟩ := A'.quotient_obj_surjective
    obtain ⟨B, rfl⟩ := B.quotient_obj_surjective
    obtain ⟨φ, rfl⟩ := (HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).map_surjective φ
    have h := upperStarTensorCounit_naturality_aux Λ f φ (𝟙 B)
    rw [CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id,
          CategoryTheory.Functor.map_id, MonoidalCategory.tensorHom_id,
      MonoidalCategory.tensorHom_id] at h
    rw [NatTrans.comp_app, NatTrans.comp_app, Category.assoc]
    exact h
